housing.graduate_housing_note: Graduate housing is allocated through an annual lottery/waitlist system; options include single-student apartments, couple residences, and family housing for students with children.

programs.name: Computer Science and Engineering (Course 6-3)
programs.department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science / Schwarzman College of Computing
programs.description: The degree chart combines programming, software construction, algorithms, computer systems, and mathematics. Students select subjects from computer science tracks and further Course 6 electives.

programs.name: Artificial Intelligence and Decision Making (Course 6-4)
programs.department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science / Schwarzman College of Computing
programs.description: The degree chart combines programming, algorithms, linear algebra, and probability with subjects across data-, model-, decision-, computation-, and human-centered AI. It also includes an application subject and advanced electives.

programs.name: Electrical Engineering with Computing (Course 6-5)
programs.department: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
programs.description: The curriculum combines programming, algorithms, discrete mathematics, and probability with system design in computation structures, electrical circuits, and signal processing. Students add coursework from electrical engineering tracks and further Course 6 subjects.

programs.name: Mathematics (Course 18)
programs.description: The degree chart requires differential equations, linear algebra, analysis, probability or statistics, an advanced mathematics subject, and six restricted Course 18 electives.

programs.name: Mechanical Engineering (Course 2)
programs.description: The core covers mechanics and materials, dynamics and control, thermal-fluid engineering, design and manufacturing, numerical computation, and measurement. Students add engineering electives and an undergraduate thesis.

programs.name: Aerospace Engineering (Course 16)
programs.description: The core includes programming, structures, signals and systems, fluid dynamics, propulsion, control, and dynamics. Later study spans several aerospace areas and includes laboratory and capstone options in flight or space systems.

programs.name: Physics (Course 8)
programs.description: The chart offers focused and flexible Physics options. The focused option includes relativity, quantum and statistical physics, experimental laboratories, a thesis, and physics and mathematics electives.

programs.name: Economics (Course 14-1)
programs.description: The program covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistical methods, and econometric data science, with advanced economics electives. The degree chart also includes a thesis option and electives in areas such as economic modeling, market design, and public policy.

programs.name: Biological Engineering (Course 20)
programs.description: The core combines organic chemistry, programming, genetics, differential equations, biomolecular thermodynamics, cell biology, and laboratory work. Later subjects cover biological systems analysis and engineering design.

programs.name: Chemical Engineering (Course 10)
programs.description: The chart combines organic chemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, transport processes, reactor design, and a project laboratory. Advanced study includes separation processes and integrated chemical engineering.

programs.name: Brain and Cognitive Sciences (Course 9)
programs.description: The core combines programming, psychology, neuroscience, neural computation, and statistics. Students complete laboratory and research work and can choose subjects in perception, neural circuits, and language.

programs.name: Management (Course 15-1)
programs.description: The curriculum combines economics, corporate financial accounting, business communication, organizational processes, and probability or statistics. Students select a management concentration and supporting electives such as operations management, marketing, strategy, or investments.

programs.name: Full-Time MBA (Master in Business Administration)
programs.description: Two-year full-time MBA. MIT Sloan lists 2026-27 annual tuition of USD 91,892, including the USD 2,200 annual programme fee; tuition for 2027-28 has not been published on the cited page.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 published annual tuition; 2027-28 tuition for 2027 entry is not yet stated on the official page

programs.name: Master of Finance (MFin)
programs.description: A 12- or 18-month graduate finance program. MIT Sloan lists 2026-27 tuition of USD 96,884 for 12 months or USD 133,007 for 18 months; rates for 2027 entry are not yet published.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 published rates: USD 96,884 for 12 months or USD 133,007 for 18 months; 2027 entry rates are not yet stated on the official page

programs.name: Master of Business Analytics (MBAn)
programs.department: MIT Sloan and Operations Research Center
programs.description: A 12-month graduate program in business analytics. MIT Sloan lists 2026-27 tuition of USD 96,884 before summer subsidy; all MBAn students receive a USD 22,000+ Capstone tuition offset. The 2027 entry tuition rate is not yet published.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 published annual tuition, excluding summer tuition subsidy; 2027 entry rate is not yet stated on the official page

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (Course 6-P)
programs.description: Internal EECS route for eligible MIT undergraduate students, combining graduate EECS coursework with an MEng thesis.
programs.tuition_status: MIT lists standard graduate tuition for 2026-27 as USD 33,360 per fall or spring term and USD 23,055 for summer 2026. MEng charges depend on registration and term; no 2027-28 programme rate is published.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate rates; not a 2027-28 quote
programs.entry_requirements: Internal program for current MIT EECS undergraduates in Course 6-1, 6-2, 6-3, 6-4, 6-5, 6-7, or 6-14; third- or fourth-year students apply before graduating. Course 6-9 students should contact BCS. Applicants should have progressed through most EECS requirements and completed at least one undergraduate research experience such as UROP. GPA figures on the department page describe most accepted students, not a minimum. Funding and thesis advising are not guaranteed.
programs.cycle: Internal MIT undergraduate application; term-specific 2026-27 calendar
required_documents: EECSIS MEng application; no separate supporting-document checklist is published on the department page.
programs.application_deadline: Term-specific: application opens on the drop date and closes on the last day of finals for each regular semester; exact 2026-27 dates follow the MIT academic calendar.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Computer Science and Molecular Biology (Course 6-7P)
programs.department: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
programs.description: The internal MEng combines graduate computer science and molecular biology subjects with a thesis and an internship. The degree chart requires a related MIT Course 6-7 Bachelor of Science earned before or alongside the MEng.
programs.entry_requirements: Only eligible current MIT Course 6-7 undergraduates may apply through the internal EECS MEng process in their third or fourth year, before graduation. EECS expects substantial progress in departmental requirements and undergraduate research experience; its typical GPA figures are not published minimums.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science (Course 6-14P)
programs.department: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science / Department of Economics
programs.description: The internal MEng combines advanced computer science and economics subjects with a thesis and an internship. The degree chart requires a related MIT Course 6-14 Bachelor of Science earned before or alongside the MEng.
programs.entry_requirements: Only eligible current MIT Course 6-14 undergraduates may apply through the internal EECS MEng process in their third or fourth year, before graduation. EECS expects substantial progress in departmental requirements and undergraduate research experience; its typical GPA figures are not published minimums.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Computation and Cognition (Course 6-9P)
programs.department: Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences / Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
programs.description: Internal five- to five-and-a-half-year program for current MIT Course 6-9 majors, combining the bachelor's and master's degrees with graduate coursework and a thesis.
programs.entry_requirements: Open only to current MIT Course 6-9 majors with a sufficiently developed research program. Published admission criteria include a technical GPA of at least 4.25/5.0, an overall GPA of at least 4.0/5.0 by the end of the application term, nine subjects or 102 units toward the major, UROP or SuperUROP experience, and a committed MIT faculty thesis supervisor. UniSearch cannot assess the two GPA minimums because the applicant profile stores one GPA normalized to a four-point scale.
programs.application_deadline: Apply in November or April; the deadline is the last day of classes for that semester. Exact dates follow the MIT academic calendar.

programs.name: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science and Engineering (Course 6 PhD)
programs.department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science / Schwarzman College of Computing
programs.description: EECS doctoral research in computer science, artificial intelligence, systems, and related fields. Funding terms are confirmed in each admission offer.
programs.entry_requirements: EECS doctoral admission is research-focused. GRE is not required. EECS lists minimum English test scores for international applicants: IELTS 7 or TOEFL iBT 100; waivers may be available under MIT policy. The department does not publish a minimum GPA.
required_documents: English proficiency exam scores for applicants to whom the requirement applies; waiver may be available
programs.application_deadline: Deadline listings conflict on the exact date; check the live application or contact the department before applying.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate full tuition per fall/spring term; summer 2026 standard rate is USD 23,055. EECS funding appointments cover full tuition for their appointment tenure.

price_facts.cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate full tuition per fall/spring term

programs.name: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering (Course 2 PhD)
programs.description: Doctoral research in mechanical engineering. The department offers research assistantships, teaching assistantships, and fellowships, but support depends on the program and individual offer.
programs.tuition_status: MIT's published standard graduate tuition is USD 33,360 per fall or spring term for 2026-27; this is gross tuition, not a confirmed 2027-28 rate or net cost. MechE research assistantships and teaching assistantships provide full tuition plus a stipend during the appointment; the department does not guarantee a package on this page.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate tuition, per fall/spring term; 2027-28 rate and individual net cost not published
programs.entry_requirements: Applicants apply directly to Mechanical Engineering for a PhD or ScD. A research-focused academic background is expected; the department publishes no minimum GPA. GRE scores are not considered except for the Naval Engineer's degree. International applicants generally need an approved English proficiency score unless they meet MIT's exemption criteria.
required_documents: English proficiency scores for applicants who do not qualify for an exemption
programs.application_deadline: December 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time for Fall 2027 entry.

price_facts.cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate full tuition per fall/spring term

programs.name: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics (Course 8 PhD)
programs.description: Doctoral research in physics. Students in good standing are typically supported through fellowships, research assistantships, or teaching assistantships, subject to the department's funding terms.
programs.tuition_status: MIT's published standard graduate tuition is USD 33,360 per fall or spring term for 2026-27; this is gross tuition, not a confirmed 2027-28 rate or net cost. Physics states its support covers tuition, health insurance, and a living stipend while students remain in good standing; confirm duration and terms in the offer.
programs.tuition_cycle: 2026-27 standard graduate tuition, per fall/spring term; 2027-28 rate and individual net cost not published
programs.entry_requirements: Apply to the Physics PhD for fall entry only. The Physics GRE is not required but is recommended. Applicants who are not eligible for an English test waiver must submit accepted English proficiency evidence. The department publishes no minimum GPA.

programs.name: Architecture (Course 4)
programs.description: The program centers on architectural design studios and techniques, with coursework in building environmental technologies, structural design, computational making, and modern architecture. The degree chart also includes restricted electives and an undergraduate thesis.

programs.name: Art and Design (Course 4-B)
programs.description: The curriculum combines design studios in objects, interaction, or information visualization with visual communication, design across scales, art and spatial practices, computational making, and design history. It also includes a research seminar and undergraduate thesis.

programs.name: Planning (Course 11)
programs.department: Department of Urban Studies and Planning
programs.description: The program combines urban design and development, public policy, microeconomics, and spatial analysis using GIS. Students build a planned set of urban studies and planning electives and complete a senior thesis or project.

programs.name: Chemical-Biological Engineering (Course 10-B)
programs.description: The curriculum combines chemistry, molecular biology, genetics, and chemical engineering. Required subjects include biochemical and chemical engineering thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, transport processes, laboratory work, and advanced chemical engineering topics.

programs.name: Chemical Engineering as Recommended by the Department of Chemical Engineering (Course 10-C)
programs.description: This department-recommended chemical engineering plan includes thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, transport processes, and differential equations. Students form a coherent program of study through restricted electives, including laboratory options across chemical, biological, materials, and related engineering areas.

programs.name: Engineering (Course 1-ENG)
programs.department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering
programs.description: The curriculum establishes foundations in programming, probability, civil and environmental engineering design, and environmental data analysis. Students choose core coursework in areas such as environmental systems, mechanics and materials, or energy, transportation, and societal systems.

programs.name: Engineering (Course 2-A)
programs.description: The core covers design, mechanics and materials, dynamics and control, thermal-fluids engineering, numerical computation, and measurement. Students complete an approved concentration of engineering electives that forms a focused area of study.

programs.name: Engineering (Course 10-ENG)
programs.description: The curriculum covers chemical engineering fundamentals, including thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, transport processes, and reaction kinetics. Students choose a concentration through related engineering and science electives and laboratory subjects.

programs.name: Engineering (Course 16-ENG)
programs.description: The core includes engineering materials and structures, signals and systems, fluid dynamics, thermodynamics and propulsion, and control or dynamics. Students build an approved concentration and complete design, testing, or development work in flight vehicles, space systems, or autonomous vehicles.

programs.name: Engineering (Course 22-ENG)
programs.department: Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering
programs.description: The curriculum combines thermal-fluids engineering and differential equations with nuclear engineering, ionizing radiation, and nuclear detection laboratory work. Students study a fission or fusion energy system and select computational and mathematics coursework.

programs.name: Materials Science and Engineering (Course 3)
programs.department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
programs.description: The program studies material structure, thermodynamics, mechanics, synthesis and design, microstructural evolution, and electronic, optical, and magnetic properties. Laboratory and processing subjects connect these topics to materials projects and manufacturing.

programs.name: Materials Science and Engineering (Course 3-A)
programs.department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
programs.description: Students follow a department-recommended plan centered on materials structure and thermodynamics, then select additional materials subjects such as mechanics, synthesis, computational methods, microstructures, properties, processing, and laboratory work. The chart requires a submitted plan of study.

programs.name: Mechanical and Ocean Engineering (Course 2-OE)
programs.description: The core combines mechanical engineering in materials, dynamics and control, thermal-fluids, numerical computation, and instrumentation with ocean-focused subjects in hydrodynamics, marine power and propulsion, and ocean engineering design and experimentation.

programs.name: Nuclear Science and Engineering (Course 22)
programs.department: Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering
programs.description: The curriculum covers nuclear engineering and ionizing radiation alongside applied nuclear physics, computation, and mathematics. Students complete laboratory and advanced electives in nuclear science and engineering.

programs.name: Anthropology (Course 21A)
programs.description: Students study anthropology through subjects on comparing human cultures, how culture works, and the meaning of life, with further anthropology electives. The chart also lists ethnography and fieldwork, and allows a thesis option developed with an advisor.

programs.name: Comparative Media Studies (CMS)
programs.description: The required curriculum begins with media studies and a media practice or production subject, with further study selected from the CMS curriculum. Chart-listed options include game design, documentary, virtual reality, spatial sound, educational technology, and digital humanities.

programs.name: Global Studies and Languages (Course 21G)
programs.description: Students follow a language-based course of study in French, German, or Spanish, combining advanced language work with cultural and humanities subjects. The degree chart presents separate requirements for each language area.

programs.name: History (Course 21H)
programs.description: The curriculum combines a history seminar, theories and methods in historical study, pre-thesis work, and a thesis. Students build a coherent elective plan across two geographical areas, including both premodern and modern history.

programs.name: Humanities and Engineering (Course 21E)
programs.description: The degree pairs a humanities field such as anthropology, history, literature, or comparative media studies with six electives from one approved engineering curriculum. The chart also lists the humanities thesis and communication-intensive requirements.

programs.name: Humanities and Science (Course 21S)
programs.description: The degree combines a humanities field chosen from the listed areas with six subjects from one approved science curriculum. The chart also includes requirements such as humanities electives and a thesis option in several fields.

programs.name: Linguistics and Philosophy (Course 24-2)
programs.description: The chart presents a linguistics track with Introduction to Linguistics and additional study across linguistics and philosophy. Listed subjects include phonology, syntax, semantics, language acquisition, logic, and philosophy of language.

programs.name: Literature (Course 21L)
programs.description: The degree centers on literature seminars in literary methods, fiction, drama, poetry, authors, film, cultural interpretation, literary history, and media in cultural context. The chart also specifies study of texts from before 1900 and intermediate or seminar-level literature subjects.

programs.name: Mathematical Economics (Course 14-2)
programs.description: The required subjects combine microeconomics and macroeconomics with statistical methods, econometric data science, real analysis, and differential equations or linear algebra. The chart also lists advanced economics options such as game theory and intermediate microeconomic theory.

programs.name: Music (Course 21M)
programs.description: The chart includes harmony and counterpoint, performance subjects, and advanced seminars in music, musicology, ethnomusicology, and music theory or analysis. Restricted electives are selected from the music curriculum with faculty guidance.

programs.name: Philosophy (Course 24-1)
programs.description: The chart requires introductory philosophy, a history-of-philosophy subject, and study in knowledge and reality. Listed choices include classics of Western philosophy, philosophy of religion, philosophical issues in brain science, and minds and machines.

programs.name: Political Science (Course 17)
programs.description: The required program includes political science scope and methods, a political science laboratory, and a thesis research design seminar with an undergraduate thesis. Students choose electives across four listed subject groups to form a coherent area of study.

programs.name: Theater Arts (Course 21T)
programs.description: The chart offers foundational subjects in acting, physical improvisation, theater design, performance media, script analysis, and playwriting. Students add theater electives selected with a major advisor.

programs.name: Writing (Course 21W)
programs.description: The chart combines a writing pre-thesis tutorial and thesis with workshops in areas such as fiction, genre fiction, science fiction, poetry, interactive narrative, and advanced fiction or poetry. It also lists writing electives, including subjects in creative nonfiction and science writing.

programs.name: Business Analytics (Course 15-2)
programs.description: Bachelor of Science focused on data modeling, optimization and machine learning for business decisions. The curriculum covers programming, probability and statistics, operations analytics and communicating with data. MIT Sloan's Fall 2026 major requirements list eight required subject areas and five restricted electives; these are degree requirements, not admission prerequisites.

programs.name: Finance (Course 15-3)
programs.description: The chart includes microeconomics or economic analysis for business decisions, laboratories in investments and corporate finance, and corporate financial accounting. Students also choose coursework in statistical methods or applied probability and statistics.

programs.name: Biology (Course 7)
programs.description: The required subjects include experimental molecular biology, genetics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, cell biology, and thermodynamics. The chart also lists a molecular biology laboratory and alternatives for several chemistry or biology requirements.

programs.name: Chemistry (Course 5)
programs.description: The standard-option chart lists inorganic and biological chemistry, two organic chemistry subjects, thermodynamics and kinetics, and spectroscopy or molecular electronic structure. It also provides options for laboratory and advanced chemistry coursework.

programs.name: Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences (Course 12)
programs.department: Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences
programs.description: The chart lists introductory coursework in geology, geophysics and planetary science, atmosphere, ocean and climate dynamics, and the global carbon cycle. It also includes laboratory or field subjects and an undergraduate thesis option.

programs.name: Mathematics with Computer Science (Course 18-C)
programs.description: The chart combines mathematics subjects such as differential equations, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, and analysis with computer science coursework. Listed subjects include mathematics for computer science, programming, and fundamentals of programming.

programs.name: Chemistry and Biology (Course 5-7)
programs.description: The required subjects combine inorganic, biological, and organic chemistry with chemical biology, thermodynamics, and spectroscopy. The chart also includes genetics and cell biology, with listed laboratory alternatives in chemistry and biology.

programs.name: Climate System Science and Engineering (Course 1-12)
programs.description: The chart includes probability and causal inference for data analysis, environmental data analysis, differential equations, and introductory programming. It also specifies climate and earth-system engineering subjects, including climate dynamics and environmental subjects.

programs.name: Computation and Cognition (Course 6-9)
programs.description: The chart combines computer science programming, neuroscience, linear algebra, and discrete mathematics or differential equations with further subjects in computation and cognition. The listed requirements include Introduction to Neuroscience and programming in Python.

programs.name: Computer Science and Molecular Biology (Course 6-7)
programs.description: The chart combines introductory programming and computer science with mathematics, molecular biology, and laboratory coursework. Listed biology subjects include genetics and cell biology, alongside chemistry and computational science options.

programs.name: Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science (Course 6-14)
programs.description: The chart combines linear algebra and computer science subjects such as programming, algorithms, and mathematics for computer science with economics and data science coursework. Its listed foundations also include econometric methods and statistical analysis.

programs.name: Urban Science and Planning with Computer Science (Course 11-6)
programs.department: Department of Urban Studies and Planning; Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
programs.description: The chart combines programming, algorithms, and computer science electives with urban planning, spatial analysis and GIS, policy, and urban technology workshops. Urban science electives include topics such as data science for cities, mobility, housing, and sustainability.

programs.name: Master of Science in Management Studies (MSMS)
programs.description: A customizable nine-month management degree for eligible current students and graduates of MIT Sloan partner or affiliate schools. It combines advanced coursework with a thesis.
programs.entry_requirements: Only current students or graduates of an institution or program on MIT Sloan's partner or affiliate list may apply. Some partners restrict eligibility to alumni or recent alumni; check the official list and your school before applying.

price_facts.cycle: 2026-27 academic year; includes mandatory Sloan program fee

programs.name: Master of Science in Aeronautics and Astronautics
programs.description: Graduate study combines advanced aerospace subjects with a research or design thesis; students can focus on areas such as propulsion, space systems, controls, or aerospace computation.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Biomedical Engineering
programs.description: A five-year MIT undergraduate pathway that combines an engineering or science bachelor's degree with graduate biomedical engineering study, linking engineering methods to molecular and genomic biology.
programs.entry_requirements: MIT undergrads only; external candidates cannot apply. Internal MEng application required; OGE department Dec 1 2026 deadline is for department graduate routes, not necessarily MEng internal submissions. Tests: Biological Engineering does not accept GRE. Internal MEng exam/ELP rules unknown. Docs: Record of Courses Taken in Preparation for Graduate Study form; full internal checklist unknown. Cost Funding: Student pays additional 12 months' tuition; support not promised. Exact internal total unknown.

programs.name: Master of Science in Building Technology
programs.description: Studies engineering principles for buildings and cities, including structural performance, construction, energy modelling, daylight, and thermal comfort; the program includes a thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering Practice
programs.description: Combines graduate chemical engineering coursework with MIT's Practice School, where students solve projects at industrial sites under MIT faculty supervision instead of writing a master's thesis.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Civil and Environmental Engineering
programs.description: A nine-month professional program built around intensive coursework and applied engineering projects, with tracks in climate and sustainability, data science for engineering systems, and structural mechanics and design.

programs.name: Master of Science in Earth and Planetary Sciences
programs.description: An individually arranged program of graduate study and research in Earth and planetary processes, using physics, chemistry, and mathematics to investigate natural systems.

programs.name: Master of Science in Atmospheric Science
programs.description: An individually arranged program of graduate study and research in atmospheric chemistry and dynamics, using physics, chemistry, and mathematics to investigate natural systems.

programs.name: Master of Science in Climate Physics and Chemistry
programs.description: An individually arranged program of graduate study and research in climate chemistry, dynamics, and paleoclimate, using physics, chemistry, and mathematics to investigate natural systems.

programs.name: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
programs.description: Studies how the structure and composition of materials determine their properties, with graduate specialization in areas such as electronic materials, energy materials, and nanotechnology.

programs.name: Fifth-Year Master of Applied Science in Mathematics
programs.description: Fifth-Year Master of Applied Science in Mathematics offered through Mathematics. Applicant scope: Current MIT students only.
programs.entry_requirements: Current MIT students only; no external application. Tests: External Math PhD GRE-optional rule does not automatically apply; internal test policy unknown. Docs: Internal checklist unknown. Cost Funding: Internal tuition/support unknown; do not inherit PhD funding.

programs.name: Master of Engineering in Manufacturing
programs.description: A 12-month professional program in manufacturing that prepares students for technical leadership in industry through advanced mechanical engineering and manufacturing study.

programs.name: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering
programs.description: Graduate mechanical engineering study combines advanced subjects with an original research, development, or design thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Ocean Engineering
programs.description: Graduate study in ocean engineering combines advanced subjects, mathematics, and an original research, development, or design thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Oceanographic Engineering
programs.description: Graduate study in oceanographic engineering combines advanced subjects, mathematics, and an original research, development, or design thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering
programs.description: Graduate study in naval architecture and marine engineering combines advanced subjects, mathematics, and an original research, development, or design thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Media Arts and Sciences
programs.description: Students investigate and create technologies that shape expression, communication, learning, and interaction, working closely with a Media Lab research adviser and completing a thesis.

programs.name: Master of Science in Nuclear Science and Engineering
programs.description: Builds broad knowledge of nuclear science and engineering as preparation for work in the nuclear field or further research; departmental topics include reactors, radiation, materials, and plasma.

programs.name: Master of Science in Physics
programs.description: A Physics SM available only by special-case admission; MIT's normal graduate Physics program leads to the PhD.
programs.entry_requirements: MIT states that admission to its Physics SM is available only in special cases, such as U.S. military officers.

programs.name: Master of Science in Political Science

steps: Contact an Imperial supervisor and obtain agreement to supervise.

scholarships_and_funding.coverage: For 2026-27, the standard annual award is GBP 5,000 for household income GBP 0–16,000; GBP 4,400 for GBP 16,001–50,000; GBP 3,300 for GBP 50,001–55,000; GBP 2,200 for GBP 55,001–60,000; or GBP 1,000 for GBP 60,001–70,000. Home MBBS students receive additional bursary in London clinical years 5 and 6; eligible care leavers and estranged students may receive an additional GBP 500.
scholarships_and_funding.description: For Home undergraduate students starting in autumn 2026 or 2027 with household income below £70,000; award is £1,000–£5,000 per year by income. Eligible students qualify automatically.
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Catalogued Imperial undergraduate courses, including integrated undergraduate degrees; Home fee status only.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Imperial undergraduate students assessed for Home fee status, with annual household income below GBP 70,000, who apply for a means-tested government loan.
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Applicants must be Imperial undergraduates with Home fee status, household income below GBP 70,000, and an application for a means-tested government loan through their regional funding body. scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Assessed each academic year based on continued undergraduate attendance, Home fee status, household income and required government-loan assessment.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: No competitive selection is published; eligible students qualify automatically after the income and fee-status criteria are met.

admission_categories.label: Stanford School of Medicine MD Admission
admission_categories.description: MD admission uses the AMCAS primary application followed by an invitation-only Stanford Supplemental Application. The current official timeline lists recurring month-and-day dates but does not name an entry cycle; verify the dates against the intended AMCAS cycle.
admission_categories.application_fee_note: Stanford requires a nonrefundable supplemental application fee, but the current official page does not state its amount. The AAMC Fee Assistance Program waiver is available only to applicants approved before the primary application.
extra_requirements: Apply through the American Medical College Application Service (AMCAS).
Submit MCAT scores through the AMCAS process; check the current cycle page for the eligible test-date window.
Submit three to six letters of recommendation through AMCAS Letters Service.
After invitation, submit Stanford’s supplemental application, required essays, fee or applicable AAMC Fee Assistance Program waiver, and all required materials through the Stanford MD portal.
Do not send transcripts or letters directly to Stanford unless requested.

Submit the USD 100 nonrefundable application fee or request a fee waiver.
